key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector enables neural solvers to maintain accuracy as viscosity decreases, without resolving the thin vorticity layer on the residual grid.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training costs for low-viscosity flow simulations by representing near-wall layers analytically rather than through fine-grid resolution.
method: Embed the asymptotic corrector in the sl-PINN trial function to capture the √ε-thick vorticity layer.
Tie the corrector amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limiting solution.
Use coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences for the residual Laplacian in sl-FVNN.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports viscosity-uniform errors over six decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests; sl-FVNN matches sl-PINN accuracy within random-seed scatter at about half the training-step cost.
watch_item: Results concern two-dimensional flows with slip boundary conditions; extension to other wall conditions or geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
